Change: v3.1 short-drama edition: added five sheets closing the gaps that single-image and comic-panel control left open once the target is vertical short drama. Params.csv is the parameter layer and deliberately holds only four kinds of quantity - length (EP_LEN_S, SEG_MAX_S, HOOK_REPEAT_S, DIALOGUE_CHUNK_S), position (SAFE_TOP_PCT, SAFE_BOTTOM_PCT, EYELINE_PCT), and tolerance (BEAT_TOL_PCT). Constraints are excluded by rule: an axis rule or a frozen anchor sentence that becomes a parameter stops being a constraint and starts reading as an option. Every key carries its own change protocol, and EP_LEN_S carries an explicit re-derivation rule plus a snapshot convention (BeatSheet_snapshot_<EP_LEN_S>s.csv recorded here), because a CSV export freezes formulas into numbers and a bare seconds table is unreadable six months later. VerticalDramaFrameRules.csv holds VF-01 to VF-10: 1080x1920 canvas lock, top and bottom exclusion bands, eye-line height, shot-size recalibration (a 16:9 medium becomes a two-shot maximum at 9:16), background re-authoring from horizontal chains to vertical stacks, two-hander staging (front-back depth or half-frame split, never equal-distance side-by-side), camera-move axis, subtitle-versus-mouth exclusion, and one universal red-line row. ShortDramaBeatSheet.csv holds seven beats B-00 hook through B-06 cliffhanger, written as Start_pct / End_pct (the invariant, hand-authored narrative judgement, never formula-generated) with Start_s / End_s / Duration_s as a derived expansion at EP_LEN_S=90, plus RULE-01: long episodes are built by repeating the template every HOOK_REPEAT_S, never by proportionally stretching B-00 to fill the episode - proportional stretch is what flattens the middle of a 180 s cut. DialogueLipSyncMatrix.csv separates the two dialogue routes that behave completely differently under retry: generation-time native audio (Sora 2, Veo 3.1, Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3) where the line is written into the prompt, versus post-pass lip-sync (Kling 3.0, driven from audio after the clip exists). It records per-family line ceiling, language support, multi-speaker capability, failure mode and workaround. CrossEpisodeIdentityLock.csv defines L0 character sheet, L1 verbatim anchor registry, L2 reference-slot role binding, L3 first-frame anchoring, L4 seed and parameter lock, L5 character LoRA, plus L6 per-episode re-anchor protocol, and RULE-01 as a cost rule: run L0-L4 always, add L5 only past roughly 30 shots per character, because below that the training cost exceeds the regeneration cost. Existing sheets extended rather than duplicated: three P0 rows appended to Checklist (vertical safe-band compliance, cross-episode anchor identity, lip-sync frame alignment), four location columns added to GenerationIterationLog (Episode / Shot ID / Beat ID / Lip-sync method), and a Proportion-baseline-binding row added to CharacterAnchors so a live-action version binds to VerticalDramaFrameRules and cannot be validated against the illustration head-to-body table. Evidence discipline: every figure I could not verify against an official source is marked [待核: 验证方式=...] rather than filled with a plausible number, and every structural default is marked [评估] with its regression path; the secondary-source model claims behind DialogueLipSyncMatrix are marked accordingly and Veo/Sora rows are marked as repo-self-attested from VideoGenerationPromptTemplate.csv. v3.0 orientation-standard edition: added two sheets closing the orientation gap left by every previous version — all prior sheets constrained WHERE a character is, none constrained WHICH WAY they point. OrientationTokenBank (19 legal tokens: facing 6 / motion_vector 9 / camera_side 4, each with an EN and ZH prompt phrase plus a counter-example) is the vocabulary layer; OrientationAndScreenDirection (3 field definitions + 8 mechanical assertions OR-01 through OR-08 + 2 control rules) is the rulebook layer. Facing tokens: toward-camera / away-from-camera / 3q-left / 3q-right / profile-left / profile-right. Motion vector tokens: enter-left / enter-right / exit-left / exit-right / lateral-left / lateral-right / advance / retreat / static — advance and retreat were renamed from toward-camera and away-from-camera so every token stays globally unique and a single lookup cannot resolve a motion token to a facing phrase. Camera side tokens: A-side / B-side / neutral / crossing. Free-text orientation is explicitly invalid input — tokens exist so that a validator can compare them, and it cannot compare adjectives. Three P0 rows appended to TemporalConsistencyChecklist (Orientation category: facing consistency / motion vector reversal / axis side) and two rows to MultiCharacterSpatialRelations (Facing assignment / Motion vector chain) so the panel checklist and the field rulebook agree. Control resolution is fixed at one orientation state per shot: frame-level orientation is not a control channel, because video models accept change points along the timeline rather than per-frame text. Also fixed a long-standing CSV defect: unquoted commas in MultiCharacterSpatialRelations line 9 (Scale perspective) made that row parse as 8 columns. Sheet count 21 to 23. Cloudflare Pages workbench synced: orientation token table inside multi-char, per-shot facing and motion_vector selectors plus a camera_side binding in the free storyboard editor, and an OR-01 to OR-08 validator with P0/P1 output.
